title: Is ‘identity revealing’ doxxing? — the ‘Crazy, I know’ branch
context: Fragment of the Wikipedia Reliable-sources Noticeboard discussion (29 Oct – 2 Nov 2026) on the ADL’s X post implying it tracks Wikipedia editors. Kept: the 10-comment tree around Levivich’s sarcastic reply to ScottishFinnishRadish plus the Masem reminder it provoked (9 voices). Left out: the parallel defamation-law subthread (CNC, NightHeron, ~2026-53221-51), the AI-detection and deprecation-mechanics branches, and the section’s other 187 comments; the tangent on POV bans (Bluethricecreamman, Slatersteven) is kept as level-0 moves without claims.

SFR is personally responsible for the ADL’s campaign, because of his ArbCom votes.

ArbCom votes do not make SFR responsible for the ADL’s tracking.

claims.span: I don't think that the answer to that is "actively attack any advocacy organization that expresses opinions about bias on Wikipedia."

weak_points.note: The pivotal word ‘doxxing’ is never defined; the argument slides between ‘the links are public’ and ‘identity exposed as an organized campaign’ — two different things.
Rests on ‘nobody has been doxxed yet’: an argument from present absence of harm that time can flip — exactly what Masem’s reminder points at.
The counterexample works only if ADL-style campaign coverage does not differ from journalistic coverage of Bronze Age Pervert; the relevant difference (purpose, targeting, scale) is never examined.
‘Interested parties will analyze us anyway’ explains that analysis happens; it does not by itself make this announcement unremarkable — the bridging step is never stated.
The causal chain ‘ArbCom bans → ADL campaign → SFR responsible’ is asserted as a jab, never argued; it is the one place the branch gets personal.
Reading Levivich’s sarcasm as a substantive rebuttal is a judgment call (conf 0.7); the ‘personally responsible’ reading depends on inferring from Mangroves’ reply that SFR sat on ArbCom.
